title: Zero-Downtime Deployments (Blue-Green & Canary)
oneLiner: Release engineering methodologies updating production software with continuous availability and instant rollback.
imagePrompt: Router traffic shifting gradually from Blue stable version to Green canary version

body.definition: Zero-Downtime Deployment deploys new application releases without interrupting active client requests by provisioning identical parallel environments (Blue-Green) or shifting a fraction of traffic incrementally (Canary).
body.whyItMatters: Eliminates scheduled maintenance windows, validates real-world performance against a small subset of users (1-5%), and enables sub-second traffic switch-back if error rate anomalies occur.
body.example:
# Kubernetes Rolling Update Strategy
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%        # Provision 25% extra pods
      maxUnavailable: 0    # Guarantee 100% baseline capacity during rollouts
body.commonPitfall: Deploying backward-incompatible database schema migrations (e.g. dropping a column still read by active Blue pods). Requires the Expand-Contract database pattern.
body.interviewAngle: Tested in SRE and DevOps interviews: readiness vs liveness probes, rolling updates vs blue-green vs canary, and metric-driven automated rollback triggers.

quickChecks.question: What is the primary advantage of Blue-Green deployment over Rolling Update?
quickChecks.answer: Instantaneous rollback capability by switching load balancer target back to Blue.

quickChecks.question: What database migration pattern must accompany zero-downtime deployments?
quickChecks.answer: Expand and Contract (Parallel Run) schema migration.

title: Dependency Injection & Inversion of Control
oneLiner: Design pattern decoupling object creation from usage by passing dependencies externally into consumers.
imagePrompt: Dependency injection container providing concrete implementations to abstracted interfaces

body.definition: Dependency Injection (DI) is a software design pattern where an object receives its dependencies from an external source (injector) rather than instantiating them directly with new.
body.whyItMatters: Achieves Inversion of Control (IoC) and SOLID's Dependency Inversion Principle. Enables isolated unit testing via mock dependencies, flexible configuration, and modular architectures.
body.commonPitfall: Service Locator anti-pattern: Having classes query a global service container directly, hiding true dependency requirements and complicating testing.
body.interviewAngle: Evaluated through SOLID principles (especially 'D'), testability, mock injection in unit tests, and lifecycle scopes (Singleton, Scoped, Transient).

quickChecks.question: Why does Dependency Injection simplify unit testing?
quickChecks.answer: Real services (like payment or DB) can be seamlessly replaced with lightweight in-memory mocks.

quickChecks.question: What is the difference between Constructor Injection and Property Injection?
quickChecks.answer: Constructor injection guarantees required dependencies exist at instantiation; property is optional/deferred.
